# Committing

## Commits

Each time you want Git to take a snapshot of your project, you create a `commit`. A good commit has:

1. A logical, focused set of changes — not everything all at once
2. A short, meaningful message — what changed, and why?

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
❌ *"Fix"*

❌ *"change colours"*
:::

::: {.column width="65%"}
✅ *"Fix legend label overlap in volcano plot"*

✅ *"Change bar graph palette to improve contrast"*
:::
:::

::: {.callout-important}
### Commit messages are notes to your future self — who will not remember what *"fixed it"* means!
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
### Commit early, commit often. Small, focused commits are far easier to understand — and to undo — than one giant commit at the end.
:::

## Bash workflow

Using the terminal, navigate to your project folder and initialise Git:

```bash
cd my_project
git init
```

Check what Git can see:

```bash
git status
```

Stage files and make your first commit:

```bash
git add filename
git commit -m "Commit message here"
```

::: {.callout-important}
### `git add .` stages *everything* in the folder. You can use this, but set up your `.gitignore` first — otherwise you may commit files you didn't mean to!
:::

## GUI workflow

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Python (VSCode)

1. Open your project folder in VSCode
2. Click the **Source Control** icon in the left sidebar (or `Ctrl+Shift+G`)
3. Click **Initialise Repository**
4. Your files appear with **U** (untracked) badges
5. Hover a file and click **+** to stage it — badge changes to **A**
6. Type a commit message in the box at the top
7. Click **Commit** (✓)

### R (RStudio)

1. Open RStudio and go to **File → New Project → Existing Directory**
2. Navigate to your project folder and click **Create Project**
3. Go to **Tools → Project Options → Git/SVN**
4. Change version control system to **Git** and click OK
5. Restart RStudio when prompted — the **Git tab** appears top-right
6. Your files appear with **?** (untracked) badges
7. Tick the checkbox next to files to stage them — badge changes to **A**
8. Click **Commit**, write a message, click **Commit**

:::
